newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 4.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Nov. 4:
LOMA LINDA, CALIFORNIA - Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole barnstormed across central California, racing against the clock and the polls in a final effort to win the White House.

WASHINGTON - Two government shutdowns, President Clinton's organisational supremacy and the president's recovery of his own emotional balance are the essential elements of his campaign for re-election.

MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE - Even if they maintain their congressional majorities in Tuesday's election, Republicans nationally will emerge sobered by the extraordinary two-year ride they have endured since their startling election victories of 1994.

WASHINGTON - MCI Communications Corp and British Telecommunications PLC announced plans to create the world's third-largest telecommunications company, in a $21 billion deal that would be the largest acquisition ever of a U.S. corporation by a foreign entity.

TARUT, SAUDI ARABIA - Shiite Moslems are sceptical of the Saudi government's focus on the radical Shiite group Hezbollah as orchestrating the bombing of a U.S. military dormitory at Khobar Towers in June.
WASHINGTON - Students at Winston Churchill High School in the Washington suburb of Potomac are doing their entire advanced placement European history class on the Internet this year.
WASHINGTON - Drug dealers are increasingly using the U.S. Postal Service to deliver their illegal drug shipments.
